meta.title: Mpox Tracker: Africa & World
meta.description: Independent, sourced mpox tracker: WHO case counts for Africa, countries with active transmission, clade Ib spread in Europe and the US, vaccines, emergency status and a dated timeline.
meta.disclaimer: This tracker summarises WHO, Africa CDC, ECDC, CDC and national health ministry reports and named news outlets. It is not medical or travel advice. If you have a new rash or sores, or think you were exposed to mpox, contact a doctor or sexual health clinic about testing and vaccination.

headline: WHO counted 1,153 confirmed mpox cases in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, most in Madagascar. CDC says sustained clade Ib spread in the US is likely.

status.label: Active · no global emergency
status.summary: WHO ended its global mpox emergency in September 2025, and Africa CDC lifted its continental emergency on 22 January 2026, but cases continue. WHO counted 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, 785 of them in Madagascar, where a clade Ib outbreak that began in December 2025 has passed 3,000 confirmed cases. Outside Africa, clade Ib is spreading locally in Europe, mostly among men who have sex with men, and CDC says sustained spread in the US is likely.

regions.note: WHO's latest six-week count (situation report 69, published 14 Sep): 1,153 confirmed cases in 11 African countries between 6 July and 16 August. The five with the most cases are shown with counts; WHO's other six had fewer each. Lighter shading marks other countries with confirmed cases in 2026 in WHO, government or UNICEF reports. A consistent 2026 total for every country wasn't available, so other countries aren't tracked here.

claims.detail: Sexual contact is a common route, but mpox spreads through close contact of many kinds, including skin-to-skin contact, touching sores or contaminated items, and close face-to-face contact. UKHSA lists household spread of clade I in countries including Belgium, Germany, Ireland and the UK.

Anyone can catch mpox through close contact. In the EU/EEA, 89% of clade I cases in the 12 months to July with full information were men who have sex with men (ECDC), but WHO also rates the risk as moderate for sex workers and others with multiple casual partners, and household spread has been recorded.

claims.claim: There is no vaccine for mpox
claims.detail: Vaccines are in use. Africa CDC says more than 5 million doses were rolled out in 16 African countries between 2024 and January 2026, and Madagascar received another 30,000 doses from UNICEF in July 2026. CDC recommends two doses of the JYNNEOS vaccine for people at higher risk.

Mpox spreads mainly through close physical contact, such as skin-to-skin contact and sex, and most people recover. WHO rates the risk to the general population as low, and it ended its global mpox emergency in September 2025.

claims.claim: A new recombinant "super strain" is more dangerous
claims.detail: WHO has reported a virus mixing clades Ib and IIb. In the first two cases, in the UK and India, illness was similar to other clades, neither patient was severely ill and no onward spread was found. WHO's overall risk assessment did not change.

claims.claim: Clade Ib is spreading locally outside Africa
claims.detail: WHO reported community transmission in countries including Germany, Spain, Portugal, Switzerland and Thailand by May 2026. ECDC counted 1,083 clade I cases in the EU/EEA in the 12 months to July, and CDC says sustained spread in the US is likely.

positions.text: 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths in 11 African countries in the six weeks to 16 August, most in Madagascar and Angola. 52,424 confirmed cases and 238 deaths in 35 African countries since January 2025.
Lifted the continental emergency after confirmed cases fell 60% during 2025, while warning that mpox remains endemic in several settings and needs continued vigilance.

More than 60 confirmed clade I cases in at least 20 states. Presumed local spread in more than 10 jurisdictions indicates a likely transition to sustained clade Ib transmission. Risk to most people in the US remains low.
22 laboratory-confirmed cases as of 22 September, 18 of them in the Western Cape. Preliminary analysis points to clade Ib in both clusters.
3,022 confirmed cases and 20 deaths since December 2025. Surveillance, testing and vaccination in affected districts have been stepped up.

timeline.title: WHO and Africa CDC declare mpox emergencies
timeline.body: Africa CDC declares its first Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 13 August. WHO declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern the next day, as the newer clade Ib spreads from eastern DR Congo to neighbouring countries.

timeline.title: WHO ends the global mpox emergency
timeline.body: WHO's Director-General says mpox is no longer a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, citing sustained declines in DR Congo, Burundi, Sierra Leone and Uganda. Africa CDC's advisory group, which met on 2 September, recommends keeping the continental emergency.

timeline.title: Locally acquired clade I cases in Europe and California
timeline.body: Spain, the Netherlands, Italy and Portugal report clade I cases in men with no travel link, and ECDC urges renewed vigilance over local clade Ib transmission. California confirms three locally acquired clade I cases, all needing hospital care.

timeline.title: Madagascar declares its first mpox outbreak
timeline.body: The first case was detected on 17 December. Institut Pasteur de Madagascar confirmed clade Ib on 13 January, and 133 cases were laboratory-confirmed by 21 January. By March, Madagascar reports more confirmed cases than any other African country (WHO).

timeline.title: India reports a recombinant clade Ib/IIb virus
timeline.body: India notifies WHO of the second known case of a virus mixing clades Ib and IIb, after one in the UK. Neither patient was severely ill and no onward spread was found. WHO says the strain is likely more widespread than documented.

timeline.title: Africa CDC lifts the continental emergency
timeline.body: After 17 months, Africa CDC ends mpox's status as a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security. It says confirmed cases fell 60% between early and late 2025 and more than 5 million vaccine doses were rolled out in 16 countries, but mpox remains endemic in several settings.

timeline.title: Comoros declares an mpox outbreak
timeline.body: By 3 February, seven cases are confirmed: five imported, mostly linked to travel from Madagascar, and two acquired locally.

timeline.title: WHO: 907 cases in 17 African countries in six weeks
timeline.body: Between 1 February and 15 March, Madagascar (368), DR Congo (288) and Kenya (78) report the most confirmed cases. Kenya accounts for 4 of the 7 deaths.

timeline.title: Madagascar passes 1,000 confirmed cases
timeline.body: WHO reports 1,092 confirmed cases and three deaths in Madagascar as of 19 April. Colombia, Denmark, Ecuador and Singapore report clade Ib for the first time.

timeline.title: WHO: clade Ib spreading locally in nine countries outside Africa
timeline.body: Colombia, Denmark, Germany, Pakistan, Portugal, Slovakia, Spain, Switzerland and Thailand report community transmission. Spain has counted 109 clade Ib cases, and Germany 74, 57 of them in 2026.

timeline.title: California reports a rise in clade I introductions
timeline.body: The state health department counts seven travel-related clade I cases in 2026, more than in 2024 and 2025 combined. Nationally, CDC had confirmed 25 travel-related clade I cases since November 2024.

timeline.title: Madagascar passes 3,000 confirmed cases
timeline.body: The health ministry reports 3,022 confirmed cases, 2,114 recoveries and 20 deaths since December. Toamasina province accounts for 40% of cases. A second batch of 30,000 vaccine doses arrived from UNICEF in early July.

timeline.title: WHO: 1,153 cases in 11 African countries in six weeks
timeline.body: Between 6 July and 16 August, Madagascar (785), Angola (184), Kenya (94), DR Congo (41) and Cameroon (28) report the most confirmed cases; 7 people died. Since January 2025, 35 African countries have reported 52,424 confirmed cases and 238 deaths.

timeline.title: South Africa reports 22 cases, likely clade Ib
timeline.body: The health department counts 22 laboratory-confirmed cases as of 22 September: 18 in the Western Cape, 3 in Gauteng and 1 in KwaZulu-Natal. Thirteen of the Western Cape cases were confirmed since mid-August, and preliminary analysis points to clade Ib in both clusters.

timeline.title: CDC says sustained clade Ib spread in the US is likely
timeline.body: CDC counts more than 60 confirmed clade I cases in at least 20 states since November 2024. Since August, more cases have had no travel link, and presumed local spread in more than 10 jurisdictions points to a likely transition to sustained transmission. CDC rates the risk to most people as low.

timeline.title: CDC: more than 80 clade I cases in at least 22 states
timeline.body: CDC's updated count is more than 80 laboratory-confirmed clade I cases in at least 22 states since November 2024, up from more than 60 in at least 20 states on 25 September. CDC says cases with presumed domestic transmission have been reported in more than 10 jurisdictions and rates the risk to most people as low.

history.text: Mpox is first identified in a person, in what is now DR Congo.
Clade IIb spreads worldwide: more than 87,000 confirmed cases by May 2023. WHO's first mpox emergency runs from July 2022 to May 2023.
Clade Ib is identified in Kamituga, eastern DR Congo.
Africa CDC and WHO declare emergencies in August. Sweden reports the first clade Ib case outside Africa.
WHO ends its emergency in September. Local clade Ib spread is found in Europe, and locally acquired clade I cases in California, in October.
Africa CDC lifts its emergency in January. Madagascar's clade Ib outbreak passes 3,000 confirmed cases.

facts.a: A newer strain of clade I monkeypox virus, first identified in eastern DR Congo in 2023. Its genetic changes point to sustained spread between people, including through sexual contact, and it has since been found on several continents.

Through close contact with someone who has mpox: skin-to-skin contact including sex, touching sores or contaminated items such as bedding, and close face-to-face contact. It can also spread within households, including to children.

A rash or sores, often with fever, headache, muscle aches, low energy and swollen lymph nodes. Symptoms usually start within a week of exposure but can take up to 21 days, and typically last two to four weeks.

Most people recover. In Africa, WHO counted 238 deaths among 52,424 confirmed cases from January 2025 to mid-August 2026. Young children, pregnant people and people with weakened immune systems, including from untreated HIV, are at higher risk of severe illness.

Yes. WHO has listed two vaccines for use: MVA-BN, given in two doses and sold as Jynneos or Imvanex, and LC16m8. They are offered mainly to people at higher risk, such as contacts of cases and, in many countries, men who have sex with men with multiple partners.
